concepts.learning_objective: Explain why simply averaging the averages of groups of different sizes gives a wrong combined average.
Use (an + bm)/(n + m) to find the combined average of two collections of data.
Recognise that the average of averages is correct when all collections have the same size.
Calculate the concentration of a mixture as total quantity of the substance divided by total quantity of the mixture.
State the weighted mean formula and its history in the work of Brahmagupta and Sridharacharya.
Interpret weights as the relative importance given to each part of the data.
Compute a weighted score such as an annual mark or a combined rating from given weights.
Analyse how the weighted mean changes when all weights are scaled or increased by a constant.
Choose between cluster-column and stacked bar charts according to the comparison of interest.
Read totals, components and shares from a stacked bar chart.

topics.title: 100% stacked bar charts as an alternative to pie charts

concepts.learning_objective: Construct a 100% stacked bar chart by converting each component into a percentage of its bar's total.
Compare 100% stacked bar charts with pie charts as ways of showing proportions.
Decide which comparisons can and cannot be inferred from a 100% stacked bar chart.
Interpret charts that are both stacked and 100% stacked because every bar has the same total.
